_comment: The `rejected` field is load-bearing. For this subject a reader's first instinct is almost
always `read the documentation`, and that instinct loses sixteen methods. Naming the wrong
source and WHY it is wrong is the whole value of a row; a row that only named the right
artifact would leave the instinct untouched.
Every `recipe` is executed by verify.py and must return something.
preamble: Direct routes to specific evidence. Rejected-source notes describe limitations, not mandatory research steps.

questions.question: How do I configure InstrumentationOptions?
rejected: hosted builder documentation
the builder methods are omitted; consult the private capture and callable public builder() route

questions.question: Which RuleInstrumentationOptions constructor do I want?
rejected: full() or phase_only()
those are the only two documented, and neither instruments a single phase; the ten per-phase selectors are on the undocumented builder

questions.question: How do I turn on result previews?
rejected: requiring a custom formatter
preview_fn None selects the default formatter; a positive preview_limit enables recording

questions.question: How do I record DataFusion metrics on the spans?
rejected: the metrics module
metrics.rs is private; record_metrics(true) on the options builder is the only switch

questions.question: Which macro do I call to instrument execution?
rejected: new_instrument_rule
it is #[doc(hidden)] and upstream says it is public only because the macros need it
InstrumentedExec::new
the type is private by design and nothing public yields one

questions.question: Which macro instruments the planning phases?
rejected: instrument_session_state
it is advertised by lib.rs and appears in NEITHER rustdoc document, hosted or private

questions.question: What arguments does the macro take?
rejected: the rendered signature
rustdoc renders a macro as its header alone; the arms carry the grammar and the body is elided at every format version

questions.question: Why does my custom field never appear on a span?
rejected: add_custom_field alone
it sets a value; a tracing span's field set is fixed at creation, so the key must also be declared in the macro as field::Empty

questions.question: Where do I register the instrumentation rule?
rejected: ignoring later rewrites
later rules can preserve or change which nodes are wrapped
questions.recipe: rg -n 'register the instrumentation rule last' content/corpus/docs/README.md

questions.question: How do I instrument the object store?
rejected: InstrumentationOptions
object-store instrumentation is a separate crate and a separate call; no option enables it

questions.question: What span names will I see?
rejected: the source
span names are macro-generated and node-dependent; the observed set comes from upstream's snapshots

questions.question: What fields does a node span carry?
rejected: a fixed list
datafusion.metrics.* is built with format!() from whatever the node reports, so the vocabulary is open

questions.question: Why does my EnvFilter receive nothing?
rejected: datafusion_tracing=info
the macros default target: to module_path!(), which expands at the CALL SITE, so the spans carry your crate's target and not this library's

questions.question: What does a preview actually look like?
rejected: the signature of pretty_format_compact_batch
four integers and a Result; nothing in it says what happens to a column that does not fit

questions.question: Which opentelemetry versions go together?
rejected: version arithmetic
the table records manifest combinations, not a universal compatibility rule

questions.question: Which DataFusion version does this release need?
rejected: the version number
it has matched DataFusion's major at every release, but the column is read from each release's own manifest rather than assumed

questions.question: How do I set up a subscriber and an OTLP exporter?
rejected: this library
it emits spans and collects nothing; until a Subscriber is installed there is no output at all

questions.question: What is my own code leaving on the table?
rejected: reading the diff
the mistakes here do not fail loudly: a rule registered too early still compiles and still traces, just not the plan you meant
